newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-MOST STOCK REBOUNDS ON QUITE DAY, NO TREND CLEAR.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-MOST STOCK REBOUNDS ON QUITE DAY, NO TREND CLEAR.

text.p: * Total trade on the Estonian bourse was 58.3 million kroons
versus Thursday's 88 million kroons.
* The Talse gained 0.21 percent to close at 272.62.
* Hansapank dominated trade to close 0.25 kroons
higher on 143.50 kroons with a turnover of 27.7 million kroons.
* Dealers said trade was solid with most stock prices
staying within a defined range and no big losers or gainers.
They said are watching for Monday's reaction with no clear
directions determined for the market.
Trade was quiet on Friday on
the Tallinn stock exchange with most banking stocks stable to
slightly higher.
The Talse strenghtened slightly by 0.21 percent to close on
272.62 kroons with 47.4 million kroons of shares traded on the
main list.
Total market capitalisation was higher at 14.6 billion
kroons compared to Thursday's 14.5 billion kroons.
"The day's trade was not very busy, but for the volumes the
prices of stock fluctuated too much," one dealer said.
"There were about seven kroons between the high and lows on
Hansapank, and this seems to be too great of a movement because
the market was not nervous, just easy to move," he added.
Another dealer said that Monday will be the day to watch as
investors have had time to consider their positions and usually
falls occur on the first day of the week.
"The main issue on the Estonia bourse is that local
investors think that all small drops will be followed by a
strong rise and it is local investors who are making the market
at present," he said.
Hansapank turned over 22.7 million kroons and was stable to
close on 143.50 kroons.
Hoiupank saw trade of 8.6 million kroons to firm
to 131.40 kroons, a gain of 1.40 kroons.
"There is still an expectation about this stock and some
investors feel it will be the next to move higher," another
dealer said.
Tallinna Pank was 1.50 kroons lower on 75.50
kroons against Thursday's 77.00 kroons.
"Tallinna Pank was within its range and the news about the
share sale by the city did not really move it far. Even if the
city sold the stake at 65 kroons, I doubt it would cause a sell
off," he added.
"However, the bigger question is who will buy the stake?"
he added.
Tallinn city government confirmed today that it will sell
off a seven percent stake in the bank, but the sale will be
outside of the market and will be by tender.
On the over-the-counter market, total trade was 10.9 million
kroons of shares with Rakvere meat plant the most
traded stock by far.
Rakvere turned over 8.1 million kroons to close 0.30 kroons
higher on 16.05 kroons.
"There were some bigger blocks traded in Rakvere this
morning, but the following trade seems more speculative," a
trader said.
-- David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom +372 630 8400
reuters@reuters.ee
